cards.t: Recommendation systems: why the Internet 'knows' you
cards.tz: 推荐系统：为什么网络比你更懂你
cards.en:
Intuition: a good shop assistant remembers what you bought last time and says 'You may like this too'. A recommendation system is a computer doing the same thing for millions of people at once.

Why companies use it: to bring users back to their site, increase website traffic, keep visitors longer and optimise user experience (and sell more).

How it works (2 steps):

  1. Track: collect your activities as big data (= huge sets of data): searches, clicks, chats, location, cookies.
  2. Predict: an AI algorithm (a set of steps the machine learnt) guesses what you will want next and shows it.

Textbook story: you chat about a trip → a social app shows overseas restaurants → a video app shows travel vlogs → a shopping app pushes travel-bag discounts.

Exam wording:

  • Recommendation systems track users' activities with big data and predict their actions with AI algorithms.
  • Benefit: personalised, relevant content; increases website traffic and sales.
  • Concern: privacy, since data are collected without users noticing; filter bubble.
cards.zh:
直觉：熟客去小店，老板记得你上次买什么，会说“这个你也会喜欢”。recommendation system（推荐系统）就是电脑同时对几百万人做这件事。

公司为什么用：把用户拉回网站、increase website traffic、让人停留更久、optimise user experience，最终卖得更多。

两步原理：

  1. Track 追踪：把你的搜索、点击、聊天、位置、cookies 收集成 big data（大数据）。
  2. Predict 预测：用 AI algorithm 推测你下一步想要什么，然后推送。

课本例子：和朋友聊旅行 → 社交平台推海外餐厅 → 视频平台推旅行 vlog → 购物 app 推旅行用品减价。

考试写法（照抄英文）：

  • Recommendation systems track users' activities with big data and predict their actions with AI algorithms.
  • Benefit: personalised content; increases website traffic and sales.
  • Concern: privacy / filter bubble.

ex.q: Mary searched for running shoes once. Now she sees shoe ads on many websites. Explain how.
ex.a:
1. Her search, clicks and cookies are collected (tracking → big data).
  2. An AI algorithm analyses the data and predicts she is interested in running shoes.
  3. The recommendation/ad system shows related products on different platforms.
ex.az:
1. 搜索、点击、cookies 被收集成大数据。
  2. AI 分析后预测她对跑鞋有兴趣。
  3. 系统在不同平台推送相关广告。

ex.q: A video app's history: travel, travel, food, travel, games. What will it recommend next and why?
ex.a:
1. Count each topic: travel 3, food 1, games 1.
  2. The most frequent topic is travel, so it predicts the user likes travel.
  3. It recommends more travel videos (see the code below).
ex.az:
1. 数次数：travel 3、food 1、games 1。
  2. travel 最多，预测用户喜欢旅行。
  3. 推荐更多旅行视频。

ex.q: A student writes: 'Recommendation systems only use big data.' What is wrong?
ex.a:
1. Big data alone is only the collected data (tracking).
  2. The prediction part is done by AI algorithms.
  3. Correct answer: big data (collect) + AI (predict); give both for full marks.
ex.az:
1. 大数据只是收集回来的数据。
  2. “预测”靠 AI 算法。
  3. 正确：大数据收集 + AI 预测，两样都要写。

ex.q: Give one benefit to the user and one concern about recommendation systems.
ex.a:
1. Benefit: saves time; shows relevant, personalised content.
  2. Concern: privacy: personal data are collected without the user noticing (or: filter bubble, over-spending).
ex.az:
1. 好处：省时间、内容个人化。
  2. 隐忧：私隐被收集；信息茧房；过度消费。

frames.en: You chat about Japan, search 'Tokyo hotels', and click a ramen photo.
frames.zh: 你聊日本、搜“东京酒店”、点了拉面照片。

frames.en: The apps store every action with time and location. Millions of users' actions together form big data.
frames.zh: 各 app 记录你的每个动作、时间和位置；几百万用户的数据合起来就是大数据。

frames.en: The AI algorithm finds the pattern 'people who talk about Japan often buy luggage' and predicts you will too.
frames.zh: AI 算法找到规律“聊日本的人常买行李箱”，预测你也会。

frames.en: You see travel vlogs, Japanese restaurants and a luggage sale. More clicks = more data, so the loop repeats.
frames.zh: 你看到旅行 vlog、日本餐厅和行李箱减价。点得越多，数据越多，循环继续。

code.src:
history = ["travel", "travel", "food", "travel", "games"]
counts = {}
for tag in history:
    counts[tag] = counts.get(tag, 0) + 1
top = max(counts, key=counts.get)
print(counts)
print("Recommend more:", top)

notes.tz: 用户点击过的主题列表（被追踪的数据）。

notes.t: An empty dictionary to count each topic.
notes.tz: 空字典，用来数每个主题出现几次。

notes.t: Go through every click one by one.
Add 1 to that topic's count (start from 0 if new).
notes.tz: 该主题次数加 1（新主题从 0 开始）。

notes.t: Find the topic with the biggest count.
Show what the system will recommend.
notes.tz: 打印系统会推荐的主题。

cards.en:
Intuition: one receipt tells you little. Millions of receipts from every shop, every second, in every format, tell you what a whole city buys. That flood of data is big data.

Definition: data are collected from many sources, including sensors in the Internet of Things (IoT) (everyday objects connected to the Internet). When the volume is big enough, the data are combined into large data sets for analysis. These data sets are big data.

VMeaningChallenge
Volumehuge amount; collected and analysed with cloudstorage of the growing data
Varietymany types: text, image, audio, video, locationintegration of different data sources
Velocitygenerated and analysed at high speedeffective and timely evaluation
Veracitydata may be uncertain / wrongdata accuracy and quality

Data are collected all the time: clicks, browsing history, cookies (small files a website stores in your browser), cache, even the clipboard. Extra V's (enrichment): value, variability, visualisation.

Exam wording:

  • Volume – large amount of data; challenge: storage of the growing data
  • Variety – wide range of data types; challenge: integration of different data sources
  • Velocity – high speed of data generation and analysis; challenge: effective and timely evaluation
  • Veracity – uncertainty of data; challenge: data accuracy and quality
cards.zh:
直觉：一张收据没什么用；全城每间店每秒、各种格式的几百万张收据，就能看出整个城市买什么。这一大堆数据就是 big data（大数据）。

定义：数据来自很多来源，包括 IoT（物联网，连上网络的日常物件）里的感应器。数据量够大时整合成大型数据集作分析，就叫 big data。

V意思挑战
Volume 量数据量巨大，用云端收集分析storage of the growing data
Variety 多样文字、图像、声音、视频、位置integration of different data sources
Velocity 速度产生和分析速度快effective and timely evaluation
Veracity 真实性数据可能不准、不确定data accuracy and quality

数据随时被收集：点击、浏览记录、cookies（网站存在浏览器的小文件）、cache、甚至剪贴板。延伸 V：value、variability、visualisation。

考试写法（照抄英文）：

  • Volume – storage of the growing data
  • Variety – integration of different data sources
  • Velocity – effective and timely evaluation
  • Veracity – data accuracy and quality

ex.q: '47% of email is spam.' Which V? State the challenge.
ex.a:
1. Spam = useless or fake data, so the data are uncertain.
  2. V = Veracity.
  3. Challenge: data accuracy and quality (filter spam before analysis).
ex.az:
1. 垃圾邮件 = 不可靠数据。
  2. Veracity。
  3. 挑战：数据准确度和质量。

ex.q: A smart city collects CCTV video, GPS of buses, tweets and air-quality numbers. Which V is shown most clearly?
ex.a:
1. Look at the data types: video, location, text, numbers.
  2. Many different types → Variety.
  3. Challenge: integration of different data sources.
ex.az:
1. 看类型：视频、位置、文字、数字。
  2. 类型多 → Variety。
  3. 挑战：整合不同来源。

ex.q: '2 million emails are sent every second.' A student answers Volume. Is this best?
ex.a:
1. The key words are 'every second': this is about speed.
  2. Best answer: Velocity (high speed of data generation).
  3. Tip: 'per second / real-time / quickly changing' → Velocity; 'billions in total' → Volume.
ex.az:
1. 关键字“每秒”说的是速度。
  2. 应答 Velocity。
  3. “每秒/实时” → Velocity；“总数很大” → Volume。

ex.q: A shop's sales database grows by 2 TB every month. Which V and what challenge?
ex.a:
1. The data keep growing in amount.
  2. Volume.
  3. Challenge: storage of the growing data (e.g. move to cloud storage).
ex.az:
1. 数据量一直变大。
  2. Volume。
  3. 挑战：储存不断增长的数据。

cards.en:
Intuition: numbers make the 4 V's feel real. You do not need to memorise them; you need to match each fact to the right V.

Fact (2021)V
4.8 billion Internet users; 5 billion Google searches a day; 1.8 billion websitesVolume
YouTube videos, tweets, Google Maps driving, Instagram photos (different kinds of data)Variety
2 million emails per second; RMB 498 billion Taobao Double 11 sales; Google changing its traffic algorithm in the pandemicVelocity
47% of email is spamVeracity

Key-word rule:

  • huge totals → Volume
  • mixed types (photo + video + GPS + text) → Variety
  • per second / real-time / changes fast → Velocity
  • fake, spam, wrong, uncertain → Veracity

Exam wording:

  • Match the scenario to the V, then state its challenge in the textbook phrase.
cards.zh:
直觉：数字让 4V 更具体。数字不用背，要会把例子配对到正确的 V。

事实（2021）V
48 亿网民、每天 50 亿次 Google 搜索、18 亿网站Volume
YouTube 视频、推文、Google Maps 导航、Instagram 照片（不同种类）Variety
每秒 200 万封电邮、淘宝双十一 4980 亿、Google 因疫情改交通算法Velocity
47% 电邮是垃圾邮件Veracity

关键字法：

  • 总数巨大 → Volume
  • 类型混杂 → Variety
  • 每秒/实时/变化快 → Velocity
  • 假、垃圾、错误 → Veracity

考试写法（照抄英文）：

  • 先配对 V，再用课本句子写挑战。

ex.q: '5 billion Google searches per day.' Which V?
ex.a:
1. It is a huge total amount.
  2. Volume; challenge: storage of the growing data.
ex.az:
1. 总量巨大。
  2. Volume。

ex.q: Google changed its traffic prediction in 2020 because traffic patterns changed suddenly. Which V?
ex.a:
1. Patterns changed fast; the model had to be updated quickly.
  2. Velocity: challenge is effective and timely evaluation.
ex.az:
1. 规律突然改变，要及时更新。
  2. Velocity。

ex.q: A student says: 'Double 11 sales of RMB 498 billion shows Volume because the number is big.' Comment.
ex.a:
1. The textbook uses it for Velocity: this huge value was generated within one day, so data arrive extremely fast.
  2. Lesson: do not pick Volume just because a number is big; look for a time word (per day / per second / during a festival).
ex.az:
1. 课本把它归为 Velocity：一天内极速产生。
  2. 不要见到大数字就答 Volume，要看有没有时间字眼。

cards.en:
Intuition: when you choose the shortest queue at a supermarket, you do not calculate everything. You use experience: 'the queue with fewer full trolleys moves faster'. That quick rule of thumb is a heuristic. AI gives machines this kind of experience-based decision making.

Rule:

  • Artificial Intelligence (AI) = the intelligence of machines, often using heuristic programs, so machines can learn from experience and make decisions like humans.
  • Heuristic (認知捷徑) = a problem-solving strategy that finds effective decisions using previous experience. Fast and good, but not guaranteed perfect.

Jobs: simple, repetitive jobs (cashiers, drivers, servers, accountants, translators) are at risk (an Oxford report: 47% of US jobs could be computerised). AI also creates jobs: AI specialist, data protection officer, robotics engineer (LinkedIn 2020 top emerging jobs). Humans can focus on creativity and higher-order thinking.

Exam wording:

  • AI is the intelligence of machines that often involves heuristic programs to allow machines to learn from experience and make decisions like humans.
  • A heuristic discovers effective decisions through previous experience.
cards.zh:
直觉：超市排队时你不会精算，只凭经验“推车少的队伍比较快”。这种经验法则就是 heuristic（认知捷径）。AI 让机器也能靠经验做决定。

规则：

  • AI（人工智能）：机器的智能，常用 heuristic programs，让机器从经验学习、像人一样做决定。
  • Heuristic：凭以往经验找出有效决定的解难策略；快而好，但不保证最完美。

工作：简单重复的工作（收银员、司机、侍应、会计、翻译）有被取代风险（牛津报告：美国 47% 工作可被电脑化）。AI 也创造新工作：AI specialist、data protection officer、robotics engineer。人类可专注创意和高阶思维。

考试写法（照抄英文）：

  • AI is the intelligence of machines that often involves heuristic programs to allow machines to learn from experience and make decisions like humans.

ex.q: Give one job at high risk from AI and one job created by AI, with reasons.
ex.a:
1. At risk: cashier: the task is simple and repetitive, and self-checkout machines can do it.
  2. Created: AI specialist: companies need people to build, train and maintain AI systems.
ex.az:
1. 高风险：收银员，工作重复，自助结账机可取代。
  2. 新工作：AI specialist，需要人建立和维护 AI。

ex.q: A map app suggests a route that is usually fast but today is slower because of an accident. Is the heuristic 'wrong'?
ex.a:
1. A heuristic uses past experience to find a good answer quickly.
  2. It does not guarantee the best answer every time.
  3. So it worked as designed; with new data (accident reports) it can learn and update.
ex.az:
1. Heuristic 用经验快速找“好”答案。
  2. 不保证每次最好。
  3. 有新数据后可学习更新。

ex.q: A student defines AI as 'a computer that follows the exact rules a programmer writes'. Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Following fixed rules only is normal programming, not intelligence.
  2. Key idea missing: learn from experience and make decisions like humans (often by heuristics).
  3. Write the full textbook definition.
ex.az:
1. 只跟固定规则 = 普通程序。
  2. 缺少“从经验学习、像人做决定”。
  3. 要写课本完整定义。

cards.en:
Intuition: a child learns 'cat' by seeing many cats, not by reading a rule book. Machine learning is the same: we show the computer examples and it works out the rules itself.

Definition: machine learning is the process of a machine training itself by reading sample data. We do not program every detail by hand; we give sample data and the computer finds patterns and builds a model (= the learnt rules that give answers).

4 steps (in order):

  1. Provide data
  2. Find patterns
  3. Generate model
  4. Obtain predictions
Traditional programmingMachine learning
Human writes rules: if red and round → appleHuman gives labelled examples; computer learns the rules

More (and better) samples usually give more accurate output. Lab 1.1 Teachable Machine: name the classes, add sample images (upload/webcam) → Train Model → test with a new image not used in training. It can learn images, sounds and poses.

Exam wording:

  • Machine learning is the process of a machine training itself by reading sample data, without programming every detail manually.
  • Steps: provide data → find patterns → generate model → obtain predictions.
  • More samples give more accurate output.
cards.zh:
直觉：小朋友看过很多猫就认得猫，不是靠背规则。machine learning（机器学习）也一样：给电脑例子，让它自己找规则。

定义：机器通过阅读样本数据自我训练的过程。不用人手编写每个细节；给样本数据，电脑自己找规律，生成 model（模型，学到的规则）。

4 步（要背顺序）：

  1. Provide data 提供数据
  2. Find patterns 找规律
  3. Generate model 生成模型
  4. Obtain predictions 得出预测
传统编程机器学习
人写规则：红色又圆 → 苹果人给有标签的例子，电脑学出规则

样本越多（越好），结果越准。Lab 1.1 Teachable Machine：命名类别、加入样本图（上传/镜头）→ Train Model → 用没用过的新图测试；可学图像、声音、姿势。

考试写法（照抄英文）：

  • Machine learning is the process of a machine training itself by reading sample data.
  • provide data → find patterns → generate model → obtain predictions

ex.q: In Teachable Machine, why must the test image NOT be one of the training samples?
ex.a:
1. The model has already seen training images, so it may simply 'remember' them.
  2. A new image checks whether it really learnt the pattern and can generalise.
  3. So testing with new data gives a fair measure of accuracy.
ex.az:
1. 训练图模型已见过，可能只是记住。
  2. 新图才能测出它是否真的学到规律。
  3. 结果才公平。

ex.q: Using the code below: samples apple 150 g, 170 g; orange 110 g, 120 g. Predict a 160 g fruit.
ex.a:
1. Provide data: the 4 samples.
  2. Pattern: similar weight → same fruit.
  3. Distances: |150−160|=10, |170−160|=10, |110−160|=50, |120−160|=40.
  4. Closest is 150 g (apple, first of the tie) → prediction apple.
ex.az:
1. 四个样本。
  2. 规律：重量相近同类。
  3. 距离 10、10、50、40。
  4. 最近是苹果 → 预测 apple。

ex.q: A student trains a cat/dog model with 3 cat photos and 300 dog photos and says the model is 'smart'. Problem?
ex.a:
1. The data are too few and unbalanced for cats.
  2. The model will guess 'dog' most of the time and still look accurate.
  3. Fix: provide more and balanced samples of each class.
ex.az:
1. 猫样本太少，数据不平衡。
  2. 模型几乎都猜狗。
  3. 要给更多、平衡的样本。

ex.q: Put in order: generate model, provide data, obtain predictions, find patterns.
ex.a:
1. Provide data
  2. Find patterns
  3. Generate model
  4. Obtain predictions
ex.az: 提供数据 → 找规律 → 生成模型 → 预测。

frames.en: Upload 50 photos labelled Cat and 50 labelled Dog.
frames.zh: 上传 50 张标为 Cat 和 50 张标为 Dog 的照片。

frames.en: The computer compares pixels: pointy ears, whiskers, long snouts…
frames.zh: 电脑比较像素：尖耳、胡须、长嘴……

frames.en: Clicking Train Model saves the learnt patterns as a model.
frames.zh: 按 Train Model，学到的规律存成模型。

frames.en: Show a new photo. Output: Cat 92%, Dog 8%.
frames.zh: 放一张新照片，输出：Cat 92%、Dog 8%。

new = 160
best = min(samples, key=lambda s: abs(s[0] - new))

notes.t: Sample data: each fruit's weight (g) with its label. This is the 'provide data' step.
notes.tz: 样本数据：重量（克）和标签。即“提供数据”。

notes.t: A new fruit the model has never seen: 160 g.
notes.tz: 一个没见过的新水果：160 克。

notes.t: Find the sample whose weight is closest to 160 (the 'pattern' = similar weight → same fruit).
notes.tz: 找重量最接近 160 的样本（规律：重量相近 → 同一种水果）。
打印预测结果（该样本的标签）。

cards.tz: 监督式与非监督式学习
cards.en:
Intuition: supervised = learning with a teacher who marks every answer. Unsupervised = sorting a messy drawer yourself; nobody tells you the groups, you just notice which things are alike.

Rule:

  • Supervised learning: humans train the computer with labelled datasets (each sample has the correct answer, e.g. 'cat'), so it learns to identify data and predict results.
  • Unsupervised learning: the computer finds patterns in unlabelled datasets and makes classifications without human guidance.
SupervisedUnsupervised
Algorithmmore explicit; improves with training data; makes informed decisionsless explicit; uses artificial neural networks for more complex problems
Training dataless; structured, labelledmore; unlabelled
Training timeshorterlonger

Shortcut: look for the word label / marked / tagged → supervised. 'Groups nobody defined' → unsupervised.

Exam wording:

  • Supervised learning trains the computer with labelled datasets.
  • Unsupervised learning identifies patterns in unlabelled datasets without human guidance.
cards.zh:
直觉：监督式 = 有老师逐题批改；非监督式 = 自己整理杂乱抽屉，没人告诉你怎么分组，你只是发现哪些东西相似。

规则：

  • Supervised learning：人用有标签（labelled）的数据集训练电脑（每个样本附正确答案，如“cat”）。
  • Unsupervised learning：电脑在没有标签的数据中自己找规律分类，无需人类指导。
监督式非监督式
算法较明确；随训练数据进步较不明确；用神经网络处理更复杂问题
训练数据较少；有结构、有标签较多；无标签
训练时间较短较长

捷径：见到 label/marked/tagged → 监督式；“没人预先定义的组别” → 非监督式。

考试写法（照抄英文）：

  • Supervised: labelled datasets.
  • Unsupervised: patterns in unlabelled datasets without human guidance.

ex.q: A bank trains a model on 10,000 transactions, each marked 'fraud' or 'normal'. Which type?
ex.a:
1. Each sample has a correct answer ('fraud'/'normal') = label.
  2. So it is supervised learning.
ex.az: 有标签 → 监督式。

ex.q: A shop groups customers by buying habits without deciding the groups first. Which type?
ex.a:
1. No labels; groups are discovered by the computer.
  2. Unsupervised learning (clustering).
ex.az: 无标签、自己分组 → 非监督式。

ex.q: A student says 'Unsupervised learning needs less data and less time, because no one labels it.' Correct it.
ex.a:
1. No labelling saves human work, but the computer must find patterns alone.
  2. So unsupervised usually needs more data and a longer training time.
ex.az:
1. 省的是人手标签的功夫。
  2. 非监督式通常要更多数据、更长时间。

ex.q: Pressing 'Report spam' on emails trains the filter. Which type?
ex.a:
1. Each report gives the email the label 'spam'.
  2. Training through manual classification = supervised.
ex.az: 用户给标签 → 监督式。

cards.t: Deep learning and artificial neural networks
cards.tz: 深度学习与人工神经网络
cards.en:
Intuition: your brain has billions of neurons passing tiny signals. An artificial neural network copies this idea with many small 'nodes' passing numbers.

Rule:

  • Artificial neural network: a set of algorithms inspired by the human brain, designed to recognise patterns. It receives, processes and transmits information like the nervous system.
  • Structure: input layer → one or more hidden layers → output layer (the result appears here). Each node links to nodes in the next layer.
  • Deep learning (enrichment): computing power has grown, so we can train networks with many hidden layers ('deep'). They find hidden connections and do things humans cannot: self-driving, Go (AlphaGo beat world champions), fraud detection.

Neural networks are used in unsupervised learning for more complex problems.

Exam wording:

  • An artificial neural network is a set of algorithms inspired by the human brain, designed to recognise patterns.
  • Input layer → hidden layer(s) → output layer.
cards.zh:
直觉：大脑有几十亿神经元互传讯号。artificial neural network（人工神经网络）模仿这个概念，用大量小“节点”传递数字。

规则：

  • Artificial neural network：受人脑启发的一组算法，用来识别规律；像神经系统一样接收、处理、传送信息。
  • 结构：input layer 输入层 → 一层或多层 hidden layers 隐藏层 → output layer 输出层（结果在这里）。
  • Deep learning（深度学习，延伸）：运算力大增，可训练很多隐藏层的网络（“深”），突破包括自动驾驶、围棋（AlphaGo）、欺诈侦测。

神经网络用于非监督式学习处理更复杂问题。

考试写法（照抄英文）：

  • inspired by the human brain, designed to recognise patterns
  • input layer → hidden layer(s) → output layer

ex.q: Name the three kinds of layer and where the result appears.
ex.a:
1. Input layer: receives data (e.g. pixels).
  2. Hidden layer(s): process data.
  3. Output layer: gives the result (e.g. 'cat').
ex.az: 输入层 → 隐藏层 → 输出层（结果）。

ex.q: Why is it called 'deep' learning?
ex.a:
1. The network has many hidden layers.
  2. More layers + more computing power → finds more hidden connections.
ex.az: 因为有很多隐藏层。

ex.q: A student writes: 'A neural network is a network of computers connected by cables, like the Internet.' Correct it.
ex.a:
1. It is not a computer network.
  2. It is a set of algorithms (software) inspired by brain neurons, designed to recognise patterns.
ex.az:
1. 不是电脑网络。
  2. 是受人脑启发的一组算法。

demo.title: A photo passes through a neural network

frames.en: Pixel values of a photo enter the input nodes.
frames.zh: 照片像素值进入输入层节点。

frames.en: Each hidden node combines signals and detects a feature, e.g. edges or ears.
frames.zh: 每个隐藏节点组合讯号，侦测特征（边缘、耳朵）。

frames.en: The output node gives the answer: 'cat 0.95'. Deep learning = many hidden layers between.
frames.zh: 输出节点给答案“cat 0.95”。深度学习 = 中间有很多隐藏层。

cards.en:
Intuition: triangle (3 sides), square (4), pentagon (5)… you instantly know the next is a hexagon (6). You spotted a pattern. AI learns to do this with data.

Definition: pattern recognition is finding similarities, relationships or patterns that help analyse and solve complex problems more efficiently. AI uses machine learning: it first identifies and categorises the data, then generates the most possible output.

Two stages (Fig. 1.6):

  1. Training: many cat and dog photos → learning → a classifier that sorts Dog / Cat.
  2. Prediction: a new photo ('What is this?') → classifier → output 'Dog'.

Three applications to learn: image recognition, speech recognition, spam detection.

Exam wording:

  • Pattern recognition is the process of finding similarities, relationships or patterns to analyse and solve complex problems more efficiently.
  • AI first identifies and categorises the data, then generates the most possible output.
cards.zh:
直觉：三角形（3 边）、正方形（4）、五边形（5）……你立刻知道下一个是六边形。你认出了规律，AI 也要靠数据学会这件事。

定义：pattern recognition（模式识别）就是找出相似之处、关系或规律，更有效地分析和解决复杂问题。AI 用机器学习：先识别并分类数据，再产生最可能的输出。

两阶段：

  1. Training 训练：大量猫狗照片 → 学习 → 分类器。
  2. Prediction 预测：新照片 → 分类器 → 输出“Dog”。

三个应用：image recognition、speech recognition、spam detection。

考试写法（照抄英文）：

  • finding similarities, relationships or patterns
  • first identifies and categorises the data, then generates the most possible output

ex.q: Triangle, square, pentagon, ? What comes next and why?
ex.a:
1. Sides: 3, 4, 5 → +1 each time.
  2. Next has 6 sides → hexagon.
ex.az: 边数 3,4,5 → 下一个 6 边，六边形。

ex.q: In which stage does the AI see the new photo the user uploads?
ex.a:
1. Training uses the labelled dataset.
  2. The user's new photo is used in Stage II Prediction.
ex.az: 新照片在预测阶段。

ex.q: A student says pattern recognition means the AI 'stores every photo and looks for an identical one'. Correct it.
ex.a:
1. The AI does not need an identical photo.
  2. It learns general features/patterns (shape, edges) in training.
  3. So it can recognise a photo it has never seen.
ex.az:
1. 不是找一模一样的图。
  2. 学的是特征规律。
  3. 所以没见过的图也能认。

frames.en: Many photos labelled Cat or Dog are given to the learner.
frames.zh: 大量标了 Cat/Dog 的照片交给学习器。

frames.en: The learner finds features of each class and builds a classifier.
frames.zh: 学习器找出每类特征，建立分类器。

frames.en: A new photo goes into the classifier → output 'Dog'.
frames.zh: 新照片进入分类器 → 输出“Dog”。

cards.en:
Intuition: zoom into a photo and you see tiny coloured squares, called pixels. To a computer, a photo is just a big grid of numbers. Image recognition finds shapes in those numbers.

How it works:

  1. Images in computers are formed by pixels.
  2. The AI gathers training data by scanning the pixels on different images.
  3. By grouping the pixels together, it finds features (edges, patterns) of each object.
  4. When the same pattern appears again, it recognises the object.

Examples: object identification, signature recognition, reverse image search, doodle recognition.

Lab 1.2:

  • Reverse image search (Google Images camera icon): upload a photo to find the product/species when you don't know the keywords.
  • AutoDraw: guesses your doodle and pairs it with artists' drawings.
  • Quick, Draw!: millions of doodles form a large data set, so the AI improves over time.

Exam wording:

  • Images are formed by pixels; the AI scans the pixels of different images, groups pixels to identify features, and recognises the object when the same pattern is detected again.
cards.zh:
直觉：把照片放大，会看到一格格小色块，叫 pixels（像素）。对电脑来说，照片只是一大格数字；影像识别就是在这些数字里找形状。

原理：

  1. 电脑中的影像由像素组成。
  2. AI 扫描不同影像的像素收集训练数据。
  3. 把像素组合起来，找出物件的特征（边缘、图案）。
  4. 再次见到相同规律时就认出物件。

例子：物件识别、签名识别、以图搜图、涂鸦识别。

Lab 1.2：

  • 以图搜图（Google Images 相机图标）：不知道关键字时上传图找产品/品种。
  • AutoDraw：猜你画什么，配上画家的图。
  • Quick, Draw!：几百万涂鸦组成大数据集，AI 越玩越准。

考试写法（照抄英文）：

  • scans the pixels on different images, groups the pixels to identify features

ex.q: Why does Quick, Draw! get better at guessing over time?
ex.a:
1. Every player's doodle is saved as new training data.
  2. Millions of doodles = a large data set.
  3. The AI learns from more samples, so its predictions become more accurate.
ex.az: 涂鸦不断成为新训练数据 → 样本多 → 更准。

ex.q: You see a fish at a market but don't know its name. Which Lab 1.2 tool helps, and how?
ex.a:
1. Reverse image search.
  2. Upload the photo; the AI compares its features with images online.
  3. It returns matching pages showing the species name.
ex.az: 以图搜图：上传照片，比对特征，得出品种名。

ex.q: A student says 'The AI recognises a cat by reading the file name cat.jpg'. Correct it.
ex.a:
1. File names are not used; a photo called IMG_001 is still recognised.
  2. The AI analyses the pixels and groups them into features.
ex.az:
1. 不看文件名。
  2. 分析像素和特征。

frames.en: The photo is a grid of numbers (pixel values).
frames.zh: 照片是一格格数字（像素值）。

frames.en: Neighbouring pixels with sharp changes form edges; edges join into shapes like ears and eyes.
frames.zh: 相邻像素急变形成边缘，边缘组成耳朵、眼睛等形状。

frames.en: The features match the 'cat' pattern learnt in training.
frames.zh: 这些特征符合训练时学到的“猫”规律。

frames.en: Output: cat (high confidence).
frames.zh: 输出：猫（高可信度）。

cards.en:
Intuition: you recognise a friend in a crowd by their face shape, eyes and smile. Facial recognition lets a computer do this by measuring faces.

Rule: facial recognition is built on image recognition. The AI captures specific features on a face (wrinkles, skin tone, distance between eyes, etc.) and detects and matches the face against a database of faces to verify the identity of a person.

Uses: tag suggestions on social media, face filters (with AR), phone unlocking, border control (e-Channel), building access.

Concerns: face data are biometric personal data: if leaked, you cannot 'change your face'; mass surveillance; discriminatory outcomes if training data are biased (lower accuracy for some skin tones).

Exam wording:

  • Facial recognition captures specific features on a face and detects and matches the human face against a database of faces to verify identity.
cards.zh:
直觉：你在人群中靠脸型、眼睛、笑容认出朋友。facial recognition（人脸识别）让电脑量度面孔来做同样的事。

规则：建基于 image recognition。AI 捕捉面部特征（皱纹、肤色、眼距等），与人脸数据库比对，以核实身份。

用途：社交平台标记建议、滤镜（配合 AR）、手机解锁、过关（e-道）、门禁。

隐忧：人脸属生物特征个人资料，外泄后无法“换脸”；大规模监控；训练数据有偏差会造成歧视性结果。

考试写法（照抄英文）：

  • captures specific features on one's face; detects and matches the face against a database of faces

ex.q: A social site suggests tagging your friend in a new photo. Explain.
ex.a:
1. The site has a database of faces from earlier tagged photos.
  2. The AI finds the face in the new photo and captures its features.
  3. It matches them against the database and suggests the closest match.
ex.az:
1. 已有标记过的人脸库。
  2. 捕捉新照片人脸特征。
  3. 比对后建议最相似的人。

ex.q: Why is a leaked face database worse than a leaked password list?
ex.a:
1. A password can be changed.
  2. Face features are biometric and permanent.
  3. Leaked face data can be misused for life.
ex.az: 密码可改，脸不可改。

ex.q: A student says facial recognition is 'always fair because it is a machine'. Correct it.
ex.a:
1. The AI learns from training data made by humans.
  2. If the data contain fewer faces of some groups, accuracy is lower for them → discriminatory outcomes.
  3. Fix: use diverse, balanced training data and test for bias.
ex.az:
1. AI 从人类数据学习。
  2. 数据偏差 → 歧视性结果。
  3. 用多元平衡数据。

demo.title: Unlocking a phone with your face

frames.en: The camera takes an image of your face.
frames.zh: 镜头拍下你的脸。

frames.en: The AI finds where the face is in the image.
frames.zh: AI 找出图中脸的位置。

frames.en: It measures features: eye distance, nose shape, jaw line.
frames.zh: 量度特征：眼距、鼻形、下巴线。

frames.en: Features are compared with the stored face. Close enough → unlock; otherwise ask for passcode.
frames.zh: 与储存的人脸比对，够相似就解锁，否则要求密码。

cards.en:
Intuition: a video is like a flip book: many still pictures (frames) shown fast. So video recognition = image recognition done on many frames, plus looking at how things move between frames.

Rule: a digital video is a collection of frames, so video recognition is similar to image recognition, but needs a more comprehensive analysis because there are multiple continuous frames. It allows video classification, object tracking and action prediction.

Main application: self-driving vehicles. They use video recognition to find the distance between the vehicle and other objects (e.g. road signs). By analysing multiple frames and combining the analyses, they can react to unexpected events and recognise road signs.

Ethics link: who is accountable if a self-driving car causes an accident?

Exam wording:

  • A digital video is a collection of frames; video recognition needs a more comprehensive analysis of multiple continuous frames.
  • Self-driving vehicles analyse multiple frames and combine the analyses to react to unexpected events and recognise road signs.
cards.zh:
直觉：视频像翻页动画：很多张静止图（frames 帧）快速播放。视频识别 = 对很多帧做影像识别，再看帧与帧之间怎样移动。

规则：数码视频是帧的集合，所以和影像识别相似，但因有多个连续帧，需要更全面的分析；可做视频分类、物件追踪、动作预测。

主要应用：自动驾驶。用视频识别判断车与其他物件（如路牌）的距离；分析多帧并综合结果，从而应对突发事件、认出路牌。

伦理：自动驾驶出事谁负责？

考试写法（照抄英文）：

  • a collection of frames; more comprehensive analysis of multiple continuous frames
  • analysing multiple frames and combining the analyses

ex.q: Why is video recognition harder than image recognition?
ex.a:
1. A video has many continuous frames, not one image.
  2. The AI must analyse each frame and combine them to see movement.
  3. So it needs a more comprehensive analysis (more computing).
ex.az: 多帧，需逐帧分析再综合，较复杂。

ex.q: A ball appears at the left in frame 1 and in the middle in frame 2. What can the system work out?
ex.a:
1. Object tracking: same ball in both frames.
  2. Direction: moving right.
  3. Action prediction: in frame 3 it will likely be on the right.
ex.az: 追踪同一个球；向右移；预测下一帧在右边。

ex.q: A student says a self-driving car 'takes one photo, finds the sign, then drives'. What is missing?
ex.a:
1. One photo cannot show speed or movement.
  2. The car analyses multiple frames continuously and combines them to judge distance and react to sudden events (e.g. a child running out).
ex.az: 一张图不够，要连续分析多帧并综合。

frames.en: Camera sees a pedestrian 30 m ahead.
frames.zh: 第 1 帧：前方 30 米有行人。

frames.en: Pedestrian now 25 m ahead and moving towards the road.
frames.zh: 第 2 帧：25 米，正走向马路。

frames.en: Comparing frames: distance shrinking, pedestrian crossing → predicts they will step into the lane.
frames.zh: 比较各帧：距离缩短、行人横过 → 预测会走进车道。

frames.en: Car slows down and stops before the crossing.
frames.zh: 车减速并在路口前停下。

cards.en:
Intuition: you know your mum's voice on the phone because voices differ in how high (pitch) and how loud (volume) they are. A computer can learn the same, after it turns sound into numbers.

How it works:

  1. Each voice has a unique waveform from its pitch (frequency) and volume (amplitude) over time.
  2. Digitalisation: the sound wave is sampled (measured at fixed time intervals) into numbers.
  3. A trained algorithm learns the features of each word's digitised waveform, detects regular patterns and identifies words.
  4. The words are converted into readable text.

Speech recognition allows computers to convert human speech into written format: voice typing, voice commands. Also: music recognition ('What's this song?' matches melody/lyrics with a database), sound recognition (fire alarm, doorbell alerts for people with hearing impairment). Digital assistants and chatbots use Natural Language Processing (NLP) to turn human language into something machines understand, then do the task.

Exam wording:

  • Voices differ in pitch (frequency) and volume (amplitude); these features are captured through digitalisation (sampling).
  • Speech recognition allows computers to convert human speech into written format.
cards.zh:
直觉：电话里你认得妈妈的声音，因为每人声音的高低（pitch 音调）和大小（volume 音量）不同。电脑先把声音变成数字，就能学会分辨。

原理：

  1. 每个声音因 pitch（频率）和 volume（振幅）随时间变化，形成独特波形。
  2. Digitalisation 数码化：按固定时间间隔取样（sampling），把声波变成数字。
  3. 训练好的算法学习每个字的波形特征，侦测规律、辨认字词。
  4. 转成可读文字。

语音识别让电脑把人类说话转成文字：语音输入、语音指令。还有音乐识别（“这是什么歌？”与数据库比对）、声音识别（火警、门铃提示听障人士）。Digital assistants 和聊天机械人用 NLP（自然语言处理）把人话转成机器明白的语言再执行。

考试写法（照抄英文）：

  • pitch (frequency) and volume (amplitude); captured through digitalisation
  • convert human speech into written format

ex.q: State the two voice features that make each waveform unique and the process that captures them.
ex.a:
1. Pitch (frequency) and volume (amplitude).
  2. Captured by digitalisation: sampling the wave at fixed intervals.
ex.az: 音调（频率）和音量（振幅），以数码化取样捕捉。

ex.q: Run the code: a wave sampled 8 times per cycle. What are samples 2 and 6, and what do they mean?
ex.a:
1. Sample 2 = 100 (the peak, loudest point upward).
  2. Sample 6 = −100 (the lowest point).
  3. The list of 8 numbers is the digital version of the sound that the algorithm analyses.
ex.az: 样本 2 = 100（波峰），样本 6 = −100（波谷）；这 8 个数字就是声音的数码版本。

ex.q: A student says: 'Speech recognition records the sound and stores it as an MP3, so the computer understands it.' Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Storing audio is not understanding it.
  2. Recognition needs a trained algorithm to find patterns in the digitised waveform and identify words.
  3. Only then is it converted into text.
ex.az:
1. 储存不等于理解。
  2. 要用训练好的算法找规律、认字。

ex.q: How does sound recognition help people with hearing impairment?
ex.a:
1. The phone listens for patterns like a fire alarm or doorbell.
  2. When matched, it alerts the user by vibration or a screen message.
ex.az: 辨认火警/门铃声，以震动或画面提示。

frames.en: You say 'Hello'. Your voice makes a sound wave.
frames.zh: 你说“Hello”，产生声波。

frames.en: The microphone measures the wave at fixed intervals (e.g. 44,100 times a second) → numbers.
frames.zh: 麦克风按固定间隔（如每秒 44100 次）量度 → 数字。

frames.en: The trained model matches the number patterns with the learnt word patterns.
frames.zh: 模型把数字规律与已学的字词规律比对。

frames.en: Output on screen: 'Hello'.
frames.zh: 屏幕输出：Hello。

code.src:
import math
rate = 8
for i in range(rate):
    t = i / rate
    v = round(math.sin(2 * math.pi * t) * 100)
    print(i, v)

notes.t: Load the maths module for sin and pi.
Sampling rate: take 8 samples in one cycle of the wave.
notes.tz: 采样率：一个周期取 8 个样本。

notes.t: Repeat for sample number i = 0 to 7.
notes.tz: i 由 0 到 7 重复。

notes.t: The time of this sample (fixed intervals of 1/8).
notes.tz: 这个样本的时间（固定间隔 1/8）。

notes.t: Measure the wave height (amplitude) at that time and round it to a whole number.
notes.tz: 量度该时间的波幅并四舍五入成整数。

notes.t: Print the sample number and its digital value.
notes.tz: 打印样本编号和数码值。

cards.en:
Intuition: what counts as 'junk' differs: one person loves shop newsletters, another hates them. So the spam filter learns from your clicks.

Spam detection: AI blocks about 100 million spam messages a day, including text spam, image-based messages, emails with hidden embedded content, and messages from newly registered domains. There is no exact definition of spam, so the AI customises the filter by recording our preferences ('Report spam' / 'Not spam'). This is training through manual classification: users give labels → supervised learning.

CAPTCHA (enrichment): a test that distinguishes humans from computers to block spam bots. Google's reCAPTCHA showed words that OCR failed to read from scanned books, so humans helped digitise books. Image tasks (street signs, house numbers) helped train image recognition for maps and self-driving. 'Everyone has been an AI trainer.'

Exam wording:

  • There is no exact definition of spam, so the AI customises the filter by recording users' preferences (training through manual classification).
  • CAPTCHA distinguishes humans from computers to block spammers.
cards.zh:
直觉：什么是“垃圾”因人而异：有人喜欢商店通讯，有人讨厌。所以过滤器要从你的点击中学习。

垃圾邮件侦测：AI 每天拦截约 1 亿封，包括文字、图片式、隐藏内嵌内容、新注册域名的邮件。垃圾邮件没有确切定义，所以 AI 记录我们的偏好来自订过滤器（“Report spam”/“Not spam”）＝ training through manual classification，用户给标签 → 监督式学习。

CAPTCHA（人机验证，延伸）：分辨人类与电脑，阻挡垃圾机械人。reCAPTCHA 用 OCR 读不到的书本扫描字，人类作答时帮忙数码化书本；图像题（路牌、门牌）帮训练地图和自动驾驶的影像识别。“人人都当过 AI 训练员。”

考试写法（照抄英文）：

  • no exact definition of spam; customises the filter by recording our preferences
  • distinguishes humans from computers

ex.q: Explain how pressing 'Not spam' improves the filter.
ex.a:
1. The click labels that email as 'not spam' (manual classification).
  2. The AI uses this label as training data (supervised learning).
  3. Similar emails will go to the inbox in future: the filter is customised to the user.
ex.az:
1. 点击 = 给标签。
  2. 作为训练数据。
  3. 以后同类邮件入收件箱。

ex.q: How did solving reCAPTCHA words help digitise books?
ex.a:
1. Books were scanned; OCR failed on some words.
  2. Those words were shown in CAPTCHAs.
  3. Many humans typed them → correct text for the books.
ex.az: OCR 读不到的字给人类输入，帮书本数码化。

ex.q: A student says 'Spam filters use one fixed list of bad words for everyone.' Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Spam has no exact definition and spammers change tricks (images, new domains).
  2. The AI learns and customises the filter from each user's preferences.
ex.az: 没有固定定义，AI 按用户偏好学习自订。

frames.en: A promo email from a new domain arrives.
frames.zh: 新域名的推广邮件到来。

frames.en: Model checks text, images, sender domain → puts it in Spam.
frames.zh: 模型检查文字、图片、域名 → 放入垃圾箱。

frames.en: You click 'Not spam' = a new label.
frames.zh: 你按“Not spam” = 新标签。

frames.en: The filter learns your preference; similar emails now go to the inbox.
frames.zh: 过滤器学到你的偏好，同类邮件以后进收件箱。

cards.en:
Intuition: a photo of a page is just pixels; you can't copy or search the words. OCR 'reads' the photo and types out the text for you.

Rule: Optical Character Recognition (OCR) converts images of printed or handwritten text (from a scanner or camera) into editable, machine-readable text. It is image/pattern recognition: character shapes are matched with learnt patterns.

In this chapter:

  • reCAPTCHA used words OCR failed to read, so humans helped digitise books.
  • Google Translate camera mode = OCR + AR: OCR reads the menu text, machine translation translates it, AR overlays the translation onto the live picture. 'Detect language' helps when you don't know the language.

Exam wording:

  • OCR converts images of printed or handwritten text into editable, machine-readable text.
  • Instant camera translation uses OCR and AR.
cards.zh:
直觉：书页照片只是像素，字不能复制或搜寻。OCR 会“读”照片，把字打出来。

规则：OCR（光符识别）把扫描或拍摄的印刷/手写文字图像转成可编辑、机器可读的文字；属影像/模式识别：把字形和学到的规律比对。

本章出现：

  • reCAPTCHA 用 OCR 读不到的字，让人类帮忙数码化书本。
  • Google Translate 相机模式 = OCR + AR：OCR 读菜单字 → 机器翻译 → AR 把译文叠在实时画面上；不知是什么语言可用“Detect language”。

考试写法（照抄英文）：

  • converts images of printed or handwritten text into editable, machine-readable text
  • OCR + AR

ex.q: Which TWO technologies does Google Translate's camera use to translate a Japanese menu on screen?
ex.a:
1. OCR: reads the Japanese text from the camera image.
  2. (Machine translation translates it.)
  3. AR: overlays the translated text onto the live image.
ex.az: OCR 读字 + AR 叠加译文。

ex.q: A school scans 500 old printed reports. Why use OCR instead of storing only the scans?
ex.a:
1. Scans are images; you cannot search or edit the words.
  2. OCR turns them into text → searchable, editable, copyable.
ex.az: 扫描图不能搜寻；OCR 后可搜寻编辑。

ex.q: A student says 'A scanner by itself gives editable text.' Correct it.
ex.a:
1. A scanner only produces an image (pixels).
  2. OCR software is needed to recognise characters and convert them into editable text.
ex.az: 扫描器只产生图像，要 OCR 才变文字。

demo.title: OCR on a photo of a menu

frames.en: Camera captures the menu: pixels only.
frames.zh: 镜头拍下菜单：只是像素。

frames.en: OCR finds the text areas and splits them into single characters.
frames.zh: OCR 找出文字区，切成单个字。

frames.en: Each character's shape is matched with learnt patterns → 'ラーメン'.
frames.zh: 字形与学过的规律比对 → “ラーメン”。

frames.en: Output text can be copied, searched or translated ('Ramen').
frames.zh: 输出文字可复制、搜寻、翻译（Ramen）。

cards.t: Applications of AI and data science (overview)
cards.tz: AI 与数据科学的应用（总览）
cards.en:
Intuition: you meet AI many times a day without noticing: autocorrect, a map's arrival time, a video feed.

Textbook list:

  • Machine translation (Google Translate)
  • Autocorrect (suggesting words)
  • Digital assistants (chatbots, voice assistants using NLP)
  • Intelligent transport system (adaptive traffic lights, ETA prediction)
  • Route planning
  • Personalised marketing
  • Facial recognition
  • Monitoring health through data from wearables
  • Expert system: gives professional advice like a human expert (e.g. medical diagnosis)

Is it AI? test: a fixed calculation (sum, average, sorting by a rule) is not AI. Recognising, predicting or learning from data is AI.

Exam wording:

  • An application involves AI if the system learns from data to recognise, predict or make decisions; a fixed calculation is not AI.
cards.zh:
直觉：你每天多次用到 AI 而不察觉：自动更正、地图到达时间、视频推荐。

课本清单：

  • 机器翻译
  • Autocorrect 自动更正
  • Digital assistants（聊天机械人、语音助理，用 NLP）
  • 智能运输系统（自适应交通灯、预计到达时间）
  • 路线规划
  • 个人化营销
  • 人脸识别
  • 穿戴装置数据监察健康
  • Expert system 专家系统：像专家一样给专业建议（如诊症）

判断是否 AI：固定计算（加总、平均、按规则排序）不是 AI；从数据学习去识别、预测、决定才是 AI。

考试写法（照抄英文）：

  • learns from data to recognise, predict or make decisions; a fixed calculation is not AI

ex.q: Is calculating a student's average exam score an application of AI? Explain.
ex.a:
1. Average = sum ÷ count, a fixed formula.
  2. No learning, no prediction → not AI.
ex.az: 固定公式，无学习预测 → 不是 AI。

ex.q: A smartwatch warns a user that their heart rhythm looks abnormal. Which application and why is it AI?
ex.a:
1. Monitoring health through data from wearables.
  2. The model learnt normal vs abnormal patterns from many users' data and predicts a problem → AI.
ex.az: 穿戴健康监察；从数据学会正常/异常规律并预测。

ex.q: A student says 'A calculator app is AI because it is clever.' Correct it.
ex.a:
1. A calculator follows fixed rules; same input always gives the same output.
  2. It does not learn from experience → not AI.
ex.az: 计算机按固定规则，不学习 → 不是 AI。

cards.en:
Intuition: big data is like a mountain of rock. Data science is the whole job of turning the rock into useful gold; data mining is the digging step that finds the gold (patterns).

Rule:

  • Data science: extracting useful information from data, i.e. processing data to obtain useful information. Data come from the Internet, often through APIs (Application Programming Interface), which let programs get data from other sources. Statistical methods then analyse trends and patterns.
  • Fields (Fig. 1.16): business understanding, data mining, data cleaning, data exploration, feature engineering, predictive modelling, data visualisation.
  • Data mining: sorting structured data to recognise patterns and establish relationships.

Flow: big data → classification → analysis → statistics → solving → knowledge → decision.

Exam wording:

  • Data science extracts useful information from data.
  • Data mining is the process of sorting structured data to recognise patterns and establish relationships.
cards.zh:
直觉：大数据像一座石山。data science（数据科学）是把石头变黄金的整个工作；data mining（数据开采）是挖出黄金（规律）的那一步。

规则：

  • Data science：从数据中提取有用资讯。数据来自互联网，常经 API（应用程序接口）取得；再用统计方法分析趋势和规律。
  • 领域：business understanding、data mining、data cleaning、data exploration、feature engineering、predictive modelling、data visualisation。
  • Data mining：整理结构化数据以识别规律、建立关系。

流程：大数据 → 分类 → 分析 → 统计 → 解决 → 知识 → 决策。

考试写法（照抄英文）：

  • extracting useful information from data
  • sorting structured data to recognise patterns and establish relationships

ex.q: A supermarket finds customers who buy nappies often also buy beer. Which field? Why?
ex.a:
1. A hidden relationship between two products was found in sales records.
  2. That is data mining: sorting structured data to recognise patterns and establish relationships.
  3. Decision: place them near each other.
ex.az: 发现产品之间关系 → 数据开采。

ex.q: A dataset has blank ages and an age of 250. Which field fixes this?
ex.a:
1. Missing and impossible values make results wrong.
  2. Data cleaning removes or corrects them before analysis.
ex.az: 数据清洗。

ex.q: A student says 'Data mining means collecting as much data as possible.' Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Collecting is the IoT/big data step.
  2. Data mining is analysing structured data to find patterns and relationships.
ex.az: 收集不是开采；开采是找规律关系。

ex.q: A company turns its sales results into a bar chart for the boss. Which field?
ex.a: 1. Showing data as charts = data visualisation.
ex.az: 数据视觉化。

frames.en: Get sales data from the shop database and weather data from an API.
frames.zh: 从数据库取销售数据，从 API 取天气数据。

frames.en: Remove duplicates, blank rows, impossible values.
frames.zh: 删除重复、空白、不合理数值。

frames.en: Find the pattern: ice-cream sales rise 30% on days above 30°C.
frames.zh: 发现规律：30°C 以上雪糕销量升 30%。

frames.en: Show a chart; decide to order more ice cream when hot weather is forecast.
frames.zh: 画图；预报炎热时多订雪糕。

cards.t: Relationship between IoT, big data, AI and data science
cards.tz: IoT、大数据、AI 与数据科学的关系
cards.en:
Intuition: think of a body. IoT = eyes and ears (senses), big data = memories, AI with data science = the brain that learns, then the brain moves the hands (automation) back through IoT.

The cycle (Fig. 1.17):

  1. IoT → Big data: collect data. The IoT connects objects (phones, watches, cars, cards, cameras) to the Internet to exchange information.
  2. Big data → AI: train model. Data are analysed by AI through data science to find underlying principles, so it can predict consumer behaviour, weather, traffic, etc.
  3. AI → IoT: automate tasks using intelligence. Humans make data-driven decisions; AI performs tasks automatically according to the results.

Enrichment: automation causes workforce transition: workers need new skills or new jobs.

Exam wording:

  • IoT collects data → big data is used to train AI models (through data science) → AI automates tasks using intelligence (through IoT devices).
cards.zh:
直觉：像身体：IoT = 眼和耳，big data = 记忆，AI + 数据科学 = 学习的大脑；大脑再透过 IoT 指挥双手（自动化）。

循环：

  1. IoT → 大数据：收集数据。IoT 把手机、手表、汽车、卡、镜头连上网交换资讯。
  2. 大数据 → AI：训练模型。经数据科学分析找出原理，预测消费行为、天气、交通等。
  3. AI → IoT：用智能自动执行工作。人类作 data-driven decisions，AI 按结果自动执行。

延伸：自动化导致 workforce transition，工人要学新技能或转行。

考试写法（照抄英文）：

  • IoT collect data → big data train model → AI automate tasks using intelligence

ex.q: Describe the cycle for an adaptive traffic-light system.
ex.a:
1. IoT: road sensors and cameras count cars every second (collect data).
  2. Big data → AI: the model learns traffic patterns and predicts queues.
  3. AI → IoT: lights change their green time automatically.
ex.az: 传感器收集 → 模型学习预测 → 自动调节灯号。

ex.q: Smart greenhouse: label each part. Sensor measures humidity; model learns best conditions; sprinkler turns on.
ex.a:
1. Sensor = IoT collecting data.
  2. Model = AI trained on big data.
  3. Sprinkler = automation via IoT.
ex.az: 感应器 IoT；模型 AI；洒水 自动化。

ex.q: A student draws the cycle as AI → IoT → big data. What is wrong?
ex.a:
1. The order starts with collecting data.
  2. Correct: IoT → big data → AI → (back to) IoT.
  3. Without data, the AI has nothing to learn from.
ex.az: 次序错，应 IoT → 大数据 → AI → IoT。

frames.en: Smart watches send heart rate data every minute.
frames.zh: 智能手表每分钟上传心率。

frames.en: Millions of users' readings form big data.
frames.zh: 几百万用户数据组成大数据。

frames.en: AI learns what a dangerous rhythm looks like.
frames.zh: AI 学会危险心律的样子。

frames.en: The watch automatically alerts the user to see a doctor.
frames.zh: 手表自动提醒用户看医生。

cards.t: Ethics of AI and data science
cards.tz: AI 与数据科学的伦理
cards.en:
Intuition: a knife can cook dinner or hurt someone. AI is the same: powerful, so we must think about who gets hurt.

Main concerns:

  • Threats to privacy: massive collection of personal data (location, clicks, faces).
  • Discriminatory outcomes: biased training data → unfair decisions (hiring, loans).
  • Liability for unintended consequences on public safety: who is accountable when a self-driving car crashes: owner, manufacturer or programmer?
  • Using AI as a weapon.

Goal: develop new technology safely and with ethical values.

Misconception: 'AI is objective because it is a machine.' No: it learns from human data and can copy human bias.

Activity 1.2 (recommendations): + personalised, discover new content; − privacy loss, filter bubble. Protect yourself: read privacy policies, limit app permissions, clear cookies, strong passwords + 2FA.

Exam wording:

  • Threats to privacy
  • Discriminatory outcomes
  • Liability for unintended consequences on public safety
  • Using AI as a weapon
cards.zh:
直觉：刀可以煮饭也可以伤人。AI 很强大，所以要想清楚会伤害谁。

主要隐忧：

  • Threats to privacy 私隐威胁：大量收集位置、点击、人脸。
  • Discriminatory outcomes 歧视性结果：训练数据有偏差 → 不公平决定（招聘、贷款）。
  • Liability for unintended consequences on public safety：自动驾驶出事谁负责（车主、厂商、程序员）？
  • Using AI as a weapon 武器化。

目标：安全并有道德价值地发展科技。

误解：“AI 是机器所以客观。”错：它从人类数据学习，会复制偏见。

活动 1.2（推荐）：+ 个人化、发现新内容；− 私隐、信息茧房。保护方法：看私隐政策、限制 app 权限、清 cookies、强密码 + 2FA。

考试写法（照抄英文）：

  • Threats to privacy
  • Discriminatory outcomes
  • Liability for unintended consequences on public safety
  • Using AI as a weapon

ex.q: An AI hiring tool rejects more women because past hires were mostly men. Which concern? One fix.
ex.a:
1. Discriminatory outcome caused by biased training data.
  2. Fix: train with balanced data, remove gender-related features, and have humans review decisions.
ex.az: 歧视性结果；用平衡数据、人手复核。

ex.q: A self-driving taxi hits a cyclist. Which concern is raised?
ex.a:
1. Liability for unintended consequences on public safety.
  2. It is unclear who is accountable: owner, manufacturer, or programmer.
ex.az: 公共安全责任谁属。

ex.q: A student argues: 'AI decisions are fair because computers have no feelings.' Rebut.
ex.a:
1. AI learns patterns from human-made data.
  2. If the data are biased, the AI repeats the bias, at large scale.
  3. So AI can be unfair; it needs checking.
ex.az: AI 从有偏见的人类数据学习，会放大偏见。

ex.q: State two ways a user can protect their privacy from recommendation systems.
ex.a:
1. Limit app permissions (e.g. location off).
  2. Clear cookies / browse in private mode; read privacy policies.
ex.az: 限制权限；清 cookies；看私隐政策。

cards.t: 3D printing: what it is and how it works
cards.en:
Intuition: a hot-glue gun drawing one thin layer, then another on top, again and again, until a cup appears. That is a 3D printer.

Rule: a 2D printer puts ink or toner on paper. A 3D printer ejects materials like plastic, metal or even food, and stacks multiple layers upon each other to make a 3D object.

Process (Fused Deposition Modelling, FDM):

  1. Draw a 3D model with 3D design software.
  2. Slice the model file into separate layers.
  3. Generate codes for the movements of the printing nozzle (噴嘴).
  4. The printer follows the codes and builds the object layer by layer.
Additive manufacturingSubtractive manufacturing
adds material layer by layer (3D printing)cuts material away from a block (carving, machining)

Exam wording:

  • 3D printers eject materials such as plastic, metal or food; multiple layers are stacked upon each other.
  • 3D model drawn → sliced into layers → codes for nozzle movement generated → printed layer by layer.
  • 3D printing is an additive manufacturing method.
cards.zh:
直觉：热熔胶枪画一层薄薄的圈，再在上面画一层，一直叠，最后变成杯子。这就是 3D 打印机。

规则：2D 打印机把墨水/碳粉印在纸上；3D 打印机喷出塑胶、金属甚至食物，一层叠一层做成立体物件。

流程（FDM 熔融沉积成型）：

  1. 用 3D design software 画 3D model。
  2. 把模型切片（slice）成一层层。
  3. 生成代码，指示喷嘴（nozzle）的移动。
  4. 打印机按代码逐层打印。
Additive 增材制造Subtractive 减材制造
逐层加材料（3D 打印）从原材料切走部分（雕刻、车床）

考试写法（照抄英文）：

  • multiple layers are stacked upon each other
  • drawn → sliced → codes for nozzle movement → layer by layer
  • additive manufacturing method

ex.q: Put in order: (P) printer builds layer by layer, (Q) model sliced, (R) model drawn in 3D software, (S) nozzle codes generated.
ex.a:
1. R – draw model
  2. Q – slice
  3. S – generate nozzle codes
  4. P – print layer by layer
Answer: R, Q, S, P.
ex.az: R → Q → S → P。

ex.q: A 2 cm tall keychain is printed with 0.2 mm layers. How many layers?
ex.a:
1. 2 cm = 20 mm.
  2. 20 ÷ 0.2 = 100 layers.
  3. Thinner layers → smoother but slower print.

ex.q: A student calls carving a wooden statue with a CNC machine 'additive manufacturing'. Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Carving removes material from a block.
  2. That is subtractive manufacturing.
  3. Additive = adding layers, like 3D printing.
ex.az: 切走材料 = 减材制造。

frames.en: Draw the cup in Tinkercad (3D design software).
frames.zh: 在 Tinkercad 画杯子。

frames.en: The slicer cuts the model into 100 thin layers.
frames.zh: 切片软件把模型切成 100 层。

frames.en: Codes tell the nozzle where to move, e.g. 'move to x=10, y=20 and push plastic'.
frames.zh: 代码告诉喷嘴去哪里，如“移到 x=10, y=20 并挤出塑胶”。

frames.en: Hot plastic is ejected; layer 1, then layer 2 on top… until the cup is complete.
frames.zh: 喷出热塑胶，第 1 层、第 2 层……直到完成。

cards.en:
Intuition: to cook a dish you can use someone's recipe, copy a dish you tasted, or invent your own. A 3D model is the same: download, scan, or build.

3D printing is more accessible and affordable today: free design tools, scanning apps, model-sharing sites, budget printers.

WayHowExample
Downloadfrom a 3D model sharing platformThingiverse
Scanuse a 3D scanner on a real objectbuilding teeth models in dentistry
Builddesign it with 3D design softwareTinkercad (easy, online), SketchUp (advanced)

Watch out when downloading: files may be copyrighted, contain design errors, or come from untrusted sources.

Exam wording:

  • A 3D model can be downloaded from a 3D model sharing platform, scanned with a 3D scanner, or built with 3D design software.
cards.zh:
直觉：做菜可以照别人食谱、模仿吃过的菜、或自己发明。3D 模型也一样：下载、扫描、建造。

现在 3D 打印更普及、更便宜：免费设计工具、扫描 app、分享网站、平价打印机。

方法做法例子
Download从 3D 模型分享平台下载Thingiverse
Scan用 3D 扫描器扫描实物牙医做牙齿模型
Build用 3D 设计软件自己设计Tinkercad（简单）、SketchUp（进阶）

注意：下载的档案可能有版权、设计错误或来源不可信。

考试写法（照抄英文）：

  • downloaded / scanned with a 3D scanner / built with 3D design software

ex.q: A dentist needs a model of a patient's teeth. Best method?
ex.a:
1. Every patient's teeth are unique, so a downloaded model won't fit.
  2. Building by hand would be slow and inaccurate.
  3. Scan with a 3D scanner → exact copy.
ex.az: 牙齿独一无二 → 用 3D 扫描。

ex.q: A beginner wants to design a name tag. Which software?
ex.a:
1. Needs a simple tool → Tinkercad (easy online 3D design).
  2. SketchUp is more advanced.
ex.az: 初学者用 Tinkercad。

ex.q: A student downloads a famous cartoon figure from a sharing site and sells prints online, saying 'it was free to download, so it's free to sell'. Problem?
ex.a:
1. Free to download ≠ free to use commercially.
  2. The character is likely copyrighted; selling copies may infringe IP.
  3. Check the licence (e.g. non-commercial) or design your own.
ex.az: 免费下载不代表可商用，可能侵权。

cards.en:
Intuition: factories are great at making a million identical cups. 3D printers are great at making one special thing: a hand that fits only you, a part needed in space today.

AreaExamples
Educationproduct prototypes (樣板), organ models, scientific equipment
Foodnutritious reconstructed food for people with difficulty swallowing, picky eaters
Textile & fashionsneaker midsoles, dresses
Spacetools, robots, spare parts, engine parts printed on site
Healthcareprosthetics (義肢), replacement organs, casts, 3D aligners
Architecturehouses, concept models, furniture
Toysspare parts, customised toys

Common idea: items that are customised, one-off or few, or hard to transport.

Exam wording:

  • 3D printing is suitable for customised, small-quantity production and for printing items on site instead of shipping them.
cards.zh:
直觉：工厂擅长做一百万个一样的杯；3D 打印擅长做一件特别的东西：只适合你的义肢、太空今天急需的零件。

领域例子
教育产品样板、器官模型、科学仪器
食物给吞咽困难人士的营养重组食物、偏食者
纺织时装波鞋中层鞋底、裙子
太空工具、机械人、零件、引擎部件就地打印
医疗义肢、替代器官、石膏、牙套
建筑房屋、概念模型、家具
玩具零件、订制玩具

共通点：订制、单件或少量，或难以运送。

考试写法（照抄英文）：

  • customised, small-quantity; printed on site instead of shipping

ex.q: Why is 3D printing especially useful on a space station?
ex.a:
1. Shipping a part from Earth takes months and costs a lot.
  2. Astronauts can print the tool/spare part on site when needed.
  3. Only raw material needs to be stored.
ex.az: 运送慢又贵，可就地打印。

ex.q: Why are 3D-printed prosthetic hands helpful for children?
ex.a:
1. Each child's hand size differs and children grow fast.
  2. 3D printing makes customised hands cheaply, so new ones can be printed as they grow.
ex.az: 订制、便宜，长大可再印。

ex.q: A company plans to 3D print 1 million identical plastic bottle caps. A student says this is the best use of 3D printing. Comment.
ex.a:
1. 3D printing is slow per item and has no advantage for identical items.
  2. For mass production, moulding is faster and cheaper per piece.
  3. 3D printing suits customised or small batches (e.g. a prototype cap).
ex.az: 大量同款用模具更快更便宜；3D 打印适合订制少量。

cards.en:
Intuition: a traditional factory needs a mould, cutting, welding, painting and many workers. A 3D printer needs one person to press START.

BenefitWhy (exam phrases)
Time-savingadditive method; faster prototyping than subtractive; rapid verification of design ideas
Lower costone-step production; cuts the cost of machining, welding, painting; reduces labour costs
Tailor-madeeasier and cheaper to make customised products without moulding
Sustainabilityreduces waste vs subtractive; reuses plastic waste as material; local production reduces shipping's carbon footprint

Note: strongest for small-scale/custom work. For mass production of identical items, moulding is still cheaper per piece.

Exam wording:

  • Time-saving: faster prototyping
  • Lower cost: one-step production, reduces labour costs
  • Tailor-made: customised products without moulding
  • Sustainability: reduces waste, local production reduces carbon footprint
cards.zh:
直觉：传统工厂要模具、切割、焊接、喷漆和很多工人；3D 打印只要一个人按 START。

好处原因（考试用语）
Time-saving增材制造；faster prototyping；快速验证设计
Lower costone-step production；省去加工、焊接、喷漆成本；reduces labour costs
Tailor-madecustomised products without moulding
Sustainabilityreduces waste；reuses plastic waste；本地生产减少运输碳足迹

注意：小规模/订制时优势最大；大量同款仍是模具便宜。

考试写法（照抄英文）：

  • faster prototyping
  • one-step production; reduces labour costs
  • customised products without moulding
  • reduces waste; local production

ex.q: Suggest TWO advantages of 3D printing a personalised birthday gift.
ex.a:
1. Tailor-made: the friend's name can be added without making a mould.
  2. Lower cost / time-saving for one item: one-step production at home.
ex.az: 订制不用模具；单件一步完成，省时省钱。

ex.q: A designer tests 5 versions of a phone stand in one week. Which benefit?
ex.a:
1. Each version is printed quickly and checked.
  2. Time-saving: faster prototyping, rapid verification of design ideas.
ex.az: 快速制作样板。

ex.q: A student writes 'Sustainability: 3D printing uses no material.' Correct it.
ex.a:
1. It does use material (plastic, metal).
  2. The point is it reduces waste (only adds what is needed, unlike cutting from a block), can reuse plastic waste, and local printing cuts shipping emissions.
ex.az: 有用材料；重点是减少浪费、回收塑胶、减运输碳排。

cards.en:
Intuition: if anyone can print anything at home, they can also print fakes and dangerous things.

ImpactDetails
Intellectual property (IP)easier and cheaper to create fakes by 3D scanning; illegal file sharing/downloading; home printing of spare parts; IP law needs updating
Community safetyprintable gun files online; undetectable plastic firearms threaten safety
Industrial revolutiongreener and cheaper in small-scale production; fiercer competition; decentralisation of production, so factory workers may lose jobs

Copyright in HK: sharing copyrighted 3D files with friends without permission is most likely infringement. Designing your own model and printing it as a gift is fine.

Exam wording:

  • IP challenges: easier and cheaper to create fakes; current IP law needs to be updated.
  • Community safety: undetectable 3D-printed plastic firearms.
  • Decentralisation of local production; fierce competition.
cards.zh:
直觉：如果人人在家都能印任何东西，也就能印假货和危险物品。

影响细节
知识产权 IP用 3D 扫描更易更便宜造假；非法分享下载；在家印零件；IP 法例需更新
社区安全网上有枪械档案；无法侦测的塑胶枪
工业革命小规模生产更环保便宜；竞争更激烈；生产分散化，工厂工人或失业

香港版权：未经许可把有版权的 3D 档案分享给朋友最可能侵权；自己设计再打印送人则没问题。

考试写法（照抄英文）：

  • easier and cheaper to create fakes; IP law needs to be updated
  • undetectable 3D-printed plastic firearms
  • decentralisation of local production

ex.q: State one potential problem of printing 3D model files downloaded from the Internet.
ex.a:
1. The file may be copyrighted: printing/sharing may infringe IP.
  2. (Also: design errors, malware/untrusted source.)
ex.az: 可能侵权；设计有错；来源不可信。

ex.q: Why are 3D-printed guns a special safety threat?
ex.a:
1. Files are shared online, so anyone can print.
  2. Plastic guns may be undetectable by metal detectors.
  3. No serial numbers → hard to trace.
ex.az: 任何人可印、金属探测器测不到、难追查。

ex.q: Which is most likely copyright infringement? (A) designing your own vase and printing it (B) sharing a paid copyrighted model with friends without permission. A student picks A because 'any printing is copying'.
ex.a:
1. A is your own design → you own it; no infringement.
  2. B copies someone else's work without permission → infringement.
  3. Answer: B.
ex.az: 自己设计无侵权；未经许可分享别人作品 → B。

cards.en:
Intuition: a photo of a mountain is flat. Standing on the mountain, you feel depth. 3D visualisation tries to give you that feeling of depth.

Rule: 3D visualisation is more realistic than images on paper, screens or cinema; people get a greater sense of depth and feel they could touch the objects.

Methods:

  • 3D glasses (red/cyan or polarised, cinemas)
  • Autostereoscopic display: 3D on a special screen without glasses
  • AR
  • VR
  • Hologram
MethodReal world?Device for viewer
VRreplacedheadset
ARadded tophone / smart glasses
Hologramadded tonone (bare eyes)

Exam wording:

  • 3D visualisation gives a greater sense of depth than 2D images.
  • VR replaces the real world; AR overlays digital images onto the real world; holograms can be seen with bare eyes.
cards.zh:
直觉：山的照片是平的；站在山上才有深度感。3D 视觉化就是要给你这种深度感。

规则：3D visualisation比纸、屏幕、戏院的影像更真实，有更强的深度感，好像伸手就摸到。

方法：

  • 3D 眼镜
  • Autostereoscopic display 裸眼 3D 屏幕
  • AR
  • VR
  • Hologram 全息影像
方法现实世界观众装置
VR取代头戴装置
AR加上虚拟物手机/智能眼镜
Hologram加上不用（肉眼）

考试写法（照抄英文）：

  • greater sense of depth
  • VR replaces; AR overlays; hologram seen with bare eyes

ex.q: Which method lets a crowd see a 3D singer on stage without any device?
ex.a:
1. No headset/phone/glasses → seen with bare eyes.
  2. Hologram.
ex.az: 肉眼可见 → 全息影像。

ex.q: A games console shows 3D on its screen without glasses. Which method?
ex.a: 1. Special screen, no glasses → autostereoscopic display.
ex.az: 裸眼 3D 屏幕。

ex.q: A student says 'AR and VR are the same; both need a headset.' Correct it.
ex.a:
1. VR replaces the real world and needs a headset.
  2. AR adds virtual objects to the real world, usually just on a phone camera.
ex.az: VR 取代现实；AR 叠加，手机就可以。

cards.en:
Intuition: put on a headset and the classroom disappears; you are standing in ancient Kaifeng. Your eyes only see the computer world, so your brain believes it.

Definition: VR is a computer-simulated environment that makes users feel they are inside the virtual world.

Type of worldMade byExample
Imagination3D models in computer-aided design (CAD) softwaredinosaurs
Replication360-degree cameras capturing real scenesa real city tour

Hardware:

  • VR headset takes over one's vision. Phone-based: uses a smartphone, cheaper. Independent: built-in processor, display, audio, more expensive.
  • Controllers: remote (navigator buttons, cheaper), motion (motion sensors, more expensive), full-body trackers (track body movement, more expensive).

Activity 1.4: watch the Qingming VR video on YouTube in split-screen mode inside a cardboard headset.

Exam wording:

  • VR is a computer-simulated environment which gives users a feeling of being in the virtual environment.
  • Imagination: 3D models by CAD software; Replication: captured by 360-degree cameras.
  • VR headsets create an immersive experience by totally taking over one's vision.
cards.zh:
直觉：戴上头戴装置，课室消失，你站在古代开封。眼睛只看到电脑世界，大脑就信了。

定义：VR 是电脑模拟环境，让用户觉得身处虚拟世界。

类型制作例子
Imagination 想象CAD 软件做的 3D 模型恐龙
Replication 复制360 度相机拍摄真实场景真实城市游览

硬件：

  • 头戴装置完全占据视线。Phone-based：用手机，便宜；Independent：内置处理器、显示、音响，较贵。
  • 控制器：remote（按钮，便宜）、motion（动作感应，较贵）、full-body trackers（追踪全身，较贵）。

活动 1.4：在 YouTube 用分屏模式看清明上河图 VR，放进纸板头戴装置。

考试写法（照抄英文）：

  • computer-simulated environment
  • Imagination: CAD; Replication: 360-degree cameras
  • totally taking over one's vision

ex.q: A museum lets HK visitors 'walk' inside the real Forbidden City. Imagination or replication? Which hardware?
ex.a:
1. Real scenes → filmed with 360-degree cameras → replication.
  2. Hardware: a VR headset (phone-based is cheaper for many visitors) + remote controller to move.
ex.az: 真实场景 → replication；头戴装置 + 控制器。

ex.q: A VR boxing game must copy the player's punches and kicks. Which controller type?
ex.a:
1. Buttons cannot copy body moves.
  2. Need motion controllers for hands, and full-body trackers for kicks.
ex.az: 动作控制器 + 全身追踪器。

ex.q: A student says a dinosaur VR world is 'replication because it looks real'. Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Dinosaurs cannot be filmed with a 360° camera.
  2. They are built as 3D models with CAD software → imagination.
ex.az: 恐龙无法拍摄 → imagination。

cards.en:
Intuition: VR is a safe 'practice room' for things that are dangerous, expensive or far away.

FieldExample
MediaVR cinema
GamingVR games
MilitaryVR soldier training
HealthcareVR surgery training
Theme parkVR roller coaster
EducationVR solar system
SportsOlympics VR live streams
MapGoogle Street View VR

Why training uses VR: virtual hands-on practice with lower risk of failure in real life; repeatable; cheaper than real equipment.

Ethics: VR 'reunions' with deceased loved ones: comfort vs emotional dependence and consent to use the person's data.

Exam wording:

  • VR provides virtual hands-on training with a lower risk of failure in real life.
cards.zh:
直觉：VR 是安全的“练习室”，用来练危险、昂贵或遥远的事。

领域例子
媒体VR 戏院
游戏VR 游戏
军事士兵训练
医疗手术训练
主题公园VR 过山车
教育VR 太阳系
体育奥运 VR 直播
地图Street View VR

训练为何用 VR：虚拟实习、降低现实失败风险；可重复；比真设备便宜。

伦理：用 VR“重聚”已故亲人：安慰 vs 情感依赖、使用逝者资料的同意。

考试写法（照抄英文）：

  • virtual hands-on training with a lower risk of failure in real life

ex.q: Give TWO advantages of training surgeons with VR instead of on real patients.
ex.a:
1. Lower risk: mistakes do not harm a real patient.
  2. Repeatable anytime, and cheaper than using real operating rooms.
ex.az: 低风险；可重复、较便宜。

ex.q: A school can't afford a trip to space. Which VR application helps, and why?
ex.a:
1. VR solar system (education).
  2. Students explore planets at scale, more engaging than a textbook picture.
ex.az: VR 太阳系，更投入。

ex.q: A student says 'VR training can fully replace real practice for pilots.' Comment.
ex.a:
1. VR lowers risk and cost, but cannot copy every real feeling (forces, real emergencies).
  2. It supports training; real flight hours are still needed.
ex.az: VR 辅助而非完全取代。

cards.en:
Intuition: you point your phone at the floor and a virtual sofa appears in your real living room. The real world stays; something digital is added.

Definition: AR is overlaying digital images and information onto our real world (e.g. furniture on the floor, a makeup filter on the face, info on AR smart glasses).

VR vs AR: VR removes the real world; AR enhances your real-world experience by adding virtual objects.

Overlay made byExample
Imagination: 3D models from computer-aided design softwarea virtual cake
Replication: captured by 3D scanninga scanned elephant toy

How it shows up: the camera recognises a marker image or surface → the 3D model is drawn on top → moving the camera shows it from different angles.

Exam wording:

  • AR overlays digital images and information onto the real world.
  • AR aims to enhance the real-world experience by adding virtual objects.
cards.zh:
直觉：手机对着地板，客厅出现一张虚拟沙发。现实仍在，只是加上数码东西。

定义：AR 是把数码影像和资讯叠加在现实世界（地板上的家具、脸上的化妆滤镜、智能眼镜上的资讯）。

VR vs AR：VR 移走现实；AR 加入虚拟物件以增强现实体验。

叠加物来源例子
Imagination：CAD 软件做的 3D 模型虚拟蛋糕
Replication：3D 扫描扫描的大象玩具

出现方式：镜头辨认标记图（marker）或平面 → 在上面画 3D 模型 → 移动镜头从不同角度看。

考试写法（照抄英文）：

  • overlaying digital images and information onto our real world
  • enhance real-world experience by adding virtual objects

ex.q: Susan scans an image with her phone and a 3D heart appears that she can view from different angles. Technology? How does it help learning?
ex.a:
1. AR: the 3D heart is overlaid on the real view after the marker is recognised.
  2. She can rotate/zoom → understands the structure better than a flat diagram; more engaging.
ex.az: AR；可多角度观察，更易理解、更投入。

ex.q: A toy shop scans a real elephant toy to show it in AR. Imagination or replication?
ex.a: 1. Made from a real object with 3D scanning → replication.
ex.az: 3D 扫描实物 → replication。

ex.q: A student says a face filter is VR 'because it is virtual'. Correct it.
ex.a:
1. You still see your real face and room.
  2. Digital items are added → AR, not VR.
ex.az: 现实仍在、加上虚拟 → AR。

demo.title: How a phone shows an AR heart

frames.en: The camera shows the real textbook page.
frames.zh: 镜头显示真实课本页。

frames.en: The app recognises the printed marker image.
frames.zh: App 辨认印好的标记图。

frames.en: A 3D heart model is drawn on top of the marker in the live view.
frames.zh: 在实时画面的标记上画出 3D 心脏。

frames.en: Walk around: the app redraws the heart from the new angle.
frames.zh: 绕着走，app 按新角度重画心脏。

cards.en:
Intuition: AR is useful when you need extra information while still looking at the real thing.

FieldExample
EducationAR 3D anatomy
Militarypilot's heads-up display (HUD)
ArchitectureAR concept models
Entertainmentface filter apps
GamingAR tower-defence games
Healthcaredental treatment with AR glasses; minimally invasive surgery with live X-ray on smart glasses
AutomobileAR repair labels/instructions
TravelAR walking directions in live view; translation
Retailfurniture preview, virtual try-on

Activity 1.5 Instant translation (OCR + AR): open Google Translate → tap Camera → choose languages → point at the menu → translation is overlaid.

Exam wording:

  • AR shows extra digital information on top of the real view, e.g. heads-up displays, AR navigation, virtual try-on.
cards.zh:
直觉：当你需要一边看着真实东西、一边看额外资讯，AR 就有用。

领域例子
教育AR 3D 解剖
军事机师抬头显示器 HUD
建筑AR 概念模型
娱乐滤镜 app
游戏AR 塔防
医疗AR 眼镜牙科；智能眼镜显示实时 X 光做微创手术
汽车AR 维修标签
旅游AR 步行导航；翻译
零售家具预览、虚拟试穿

活动 1.5 即时翻译（OCR + AR）：开 Google Translate → Camera → 选语言 → 对准菜单 → 译文叠在画面上。

考试写法（照抄英文）：

  • extra digital information on top of the real view

ex.q: A fashion brand closes stores and offers AR try-on in its app. One drawback?
ex.a:
1. Customers cannot feel the material or check the real fit.
  2. (Also: digital divide for people without suitable phones; privacy of face/body data.)
ex.az: 摸不到质料、尺码不准；数码鸿沟；私隐。

ex.q: Why is a HUD useful for a pilot?
ex.a:
1. Flight data are shown on the glass in front of the pilot.
  2. The pilot keeps looking outside while reading data → safer, faster reactions.
ex.az: 不用低头看仪表，更安全。

ex.q: A student says AR walking directions need a VR headset. Correct it.
ex.a:
1. AR walking directions run on a normal phone in live camera view.
  2. Arrows are overlaid on the real street; a VR headset would block the real world (dangerous).
ex.az: 手机实时画面即可；VR 会挡住现实。

cards.en:
Intuition: a ghost-like 3D image floating on stage that the whole audience sees, with no glasses or phones.

Rule: unlike VR and AR, virtual images produced by holograms can be seen with bare eyes: no headset, glasses or screen to hold. Examples: Star Wars hologram at Walt Disney World; Michael Jackson hologram at the Billboard Music Awards.

Activity 1.6 DIY hologram pyramid: a transparent pyramid reflects the video shown on the screen.

  1. Make a pyramid from a plastic bottle/sheet.
  2. Play a hologram video: four copies of the object (one per side) on a black background.
  3. Put the pyramid on the screen; each face reflects one copy, so a floating 3D-looking object appears in the middle.

Exam wording:

  • Virtual images produced by holograms can be seen with bare eyes.
  • A holographic pyramid creates the image by a transparent pyramid reflecting the video shown on the screen.
cards.zh:
直觉：舞台上浮着一个像幽灵的立体影像，全场观众不用眼镜或手机都看到。

规则：与 VR、AR 不同，全息影像可用肉眼看到，不用头戴装置、眼镜或手机。例子：迪士尼星战全息影像；Billboard 音乐颁奖礼的 Michael Jackson 全息影像。

活动 1.6 自制全息金字塔：透明金字塔反射屏幕上的视频。

  1. 用胶樽/胶片做金字塔。
  2. 播放全息视频：黑底上有四个同一物件（每边一个）。
  3. 把金字塔放在屏幕上，每面反射一份，中间出现浮空立体影像。

考试写法（照抄英文）：

  • can be seen with bare eyes
  • a transparent pyramid reflecting the video shown on the screen

ex.q: Why does a hologram video show four copies of the object?
ex.a:
1. The pyramid has four sides.
  2. Each side reflects one copy towards a viewer on that side.
  3. Together they make the object seem to float in the middle, visible from all around.
ex.az: 四面各反射一份，四周都看到。

ex.q: A concert wants 10,000 fans to see a 3D performer at once. VR, AR or hologram?
ex.a:
1. Giving 10,000 headsets/phones is impractical.
  2. Hologram: seen with bare eyes by everyone → hologram.
ex.az: 全场肉眼可见 → hologram。

ex.q: A student says 'A face filter on Instagram is a hologram because it looks 3D.' Correct it.
ex.a:
1. The filter is seen only through the phone screen.
  2. It is AR; a hologram is seen with bare eyes without a device.
ex.az: 要透过手机看 → AR。

frames.en: The screen shows four copies of a spinning dolphin on black.
frames.zh: 屏幕黑底上有四个旋转海豚。

frames.en: A clear pyramid is placed upside down in the centre.
frames.zh: 透明金字塔倒放在中间。

frames.en: Each face reflects the copy below it at 45°.
frames.zh: 每个斜面以 45° 反射下方那份影像。

frames.en: The reflections meet in the middle: a 3D-looking dolphin floats, seen with bare eyes.
frames.zh: 反射在中间汇合：肉眼看到浮空的立体海豚。

cards.en:
Intuition: a VR field trip is cheap and safe, but if you wear the headset while walking you might hit a wall.

BenefitsLimitations
  • Virtual hands-on training and lower risk of failure in real life
  • More flexible: anytime and anywhere
  • Lower cost
  • Digital divide caused by inability to access the devices
  • Privacy and security concerns about data collection by AR (camera, location, face)
  • Being less aware of the surroundings
  • Technical expertise is required

Prolonged VR use: eye strain, dizziness/motion sickness, addiction, less real social contact. Uploading selfies/body measurements to VR platforms → privacy leakage, identity theft, misuse of personal data.

Education: AR/VR give alternatives to field trips and experiments and increase engagement. Widening the digital divide is a drawback, not a benefit.

Exam wording:

  • Benefits: virtual hands-on training with lower risk of failure; more flexible, anytime and anywhere; lower cost.
  • Limitations: digital divide; privacy and security concerns about data collection by AR; less aware of surroundings; technical expertise required.
cards.zh:
直觉：VR 考察便宜又安全；但戴着头戴装置走路可能撞墙。

好处限制
  • 虚拟实习、降低现实失败风险
  • 更灵活：随时随地
  • 成本较低
  • Digital divide 数码鸿沟：有人买不起装置
  • AR 收集数据的私隐和保安问题（镜头、位置、人脸）
  • 对周围环境警觉性降低
  • 需要技术知识

长时间用 VR：眼疲劳、晕眩、沉迷、少了真实社交；上传自拍/身体尺寸 → 私隐外泄、身份盗窃、个人资料被滥用。

教育：AR/VR 可代替实地考察和实验、提高投入度；扩大数码鸿沟是缺点不是好处。

考试写法（照抄英文）：

  • virtual hands-on training; anytime and anywhere; lower cost
  • digital divide; privacy and security concerns; less aware of the surroundings; technical expertise required

ex.q: State TWO possible risks of using a VR headset for 6 hours a day.
ex.a:
1. Health: eye strain, dizziness/motion sickness.
  2. Social: addiction and less real-life social contact.
ex.az: 眼疲劳/晕眩；沉迷、少社交。

ex.q: A VR fitness app asks users to upload selfies and body measurements. One concern?
ex.a:
1. Sensitive personal data stored online.
  2. Risk of privacy leakage / identity theft / misuse of personal data if hacked or sold.
ex.az: 私隐外泄、身份盗窃。

ex.q: A student lists 'reduces the digital divide' as a benefit of VR lessons. Correct it.
ex.a:
1. VR needs costly devices; poorer students may not have them.
  2. So VR can widen the digital divide: it is a limitation.
ex.az: VR 装置昂贵，会扩大数码鸿沟，是限制。

cards.t: Lab and activity summary: hands-on tools
cards.tz: 实验与活动总结：动手工具
cards.en:
Intuition: each lab is a small experiment showing one idea. If you remember the tool, you remember the concept.

TaskToolConcept shown
Lab 1.1Teachable MachineMachine learning: provide data → train → test
Lab 1.2 M1Google Images (search by image)Image recognition
Lab 1.2 M2/M3AutoDraw, Quick, Draw!Doodle recognition; large data sets improve AI

Activity 1.3Tinkercad, SketchUp, Thingiverse3D modelling and printing
Activity 1.4YouTube VR + cardboard headsetVR
Activity 1.5Google Translate cameraOCR + AR
Activity 1.6Holographic pyramidHologram

Exam wording:

  • Recognise the application of 3D printing, AR and VR through practical experience.
cards.zh:
直觉：每个实验都是展示一个概念的小试验；记得工具就记得概念。

任务工具概念
Lab 1.1Teachable Machine机器学习：提供数据 → 训练 → 测试
Lab 1.2 M1Google 以图搜图影像识别
Lab 1.2 M2/M3AutoDraw、Quick, Draw!涂鸦识别；大数据令 AI 进步
Lab 1.3Google Assistant 认歌语音和音乐识别
活动 1.3Tinkercad、SketchUp、Thingiverse3D 建模和打印
活动 1.4YouTube VR + 纸板头戴VR
活动 1.5Google Translate 相机OCR + AR
活动 1.6全息金字塔Hologram

考试写法（照抄英文）：

  • Recognise the application of 3D printing, AR and VR through practical experience.

ex.q: Which tool would you use to show classmates that more samples improve an AI model?
ex.a:
1. Teachable Machine.
  2. Train with 5 images per class, test; then with 50 per class, test again.
  3. Accuracy improves → more samples give more accurate output.
ex.az: Teachable Machine：少样本 vs 多样本比较准确度。

ex.q: Which activity demonstrates OCR, and what else does it use?
ex.a:
